title: Fix the cash-flow categories
prompt: The budgeting app sorts each transaction into a cash-flow category, but refunds show up as income and transactions with no direction are counted as spending. Fix `solve(transactions)`.
rules: A `credit` is `refund` when its `txn_type` is `refund`, and `income` otherwise.
A `debit` is `bank_fee` when its `txn_type` is `fee`, and `spending` otherwise.
A transaction whose `direction` is missing, or is anything but `debit` or `credit`, is `unknown`, whatever its type.
Return `transaction_id`, `txn_type`, `direction` and `category`, in that order, for every transaction.
hints: Run the starter and find the refund in the sample: it says `income`. Which `when` does a refund pass first?
The first true condition wins, so a narrow case like a refund has to come before the broad `direction == "credit"`.

`otherwise` catches every row nothing else matched, including a missing direction. Give `spending` its own `when` on debits, and keep `otherwise` for `unknown`. Check the fee rule on a row with no direction too.
explanation: Two bugs. First, the order: a refund is a credit, so it passes `direction == "credit"` and stops at `income` before the refund test is ever reached. The narrow case must come first. Second, `otherwise("spending")` catches every row nothing matched, including a missing direction. The fix tests each case on its direction and leaves `otherwise` for `unknown`: `F.when((F.col("direction") == "credit") & (F.col("txn_type") == "refund"), "refund").when(F.col("direction") == "credit", "income").when((F.col("direction") == "debit") & (F.col("txn_type") == "fee"), "bank_fee").when(F.col("direction") == "debit", "spending").otherwise("unknown")`. Testing the direction in the fee rule matters too: a fee with no direction is `unknown`, not `bank_fee`.
